lucy: Deploying a Cloudflare Worker that does `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference-js'` and it crashes at runtime: `Uncaught ReferenceError: require is not defined`. Bundle also contains a large node buffer polyfill which blows up size. Anyone seen this exact pattern?

ben: Yep. Usually means package resolution pulled CJS/node entry. Quick check: what's your package.json exports and are you bundling with esbuild/wrangler?

lucy: Using wrangler + esbuild default config. package.json just has "main" pointing at dist/index.cjs and "module" to dist/index.mjs. No explicit exports field.

harrison: That explains it. Without an "exports" map bundlers sometimes prefer CJS. Two non-controversial fixes: 1) add an explicit exports object with a clear browser/edge entry; 2) publish an explicit subpath "/edge" that consumers can import to avoid ambiguity.

ben: Example exports snippet we use:```json
"exports":{
  ".":{
    "node":"./dist/index.node.cjs",
    "import":"./dist/index.mjs",
    "browser":"./dist/index.edge.mjs"
  },
  "./edge":{
    "import":"./dist/index.edge.mjs"
  }
}```
That gets most bundlers to pick the edge build; consumers can still `import '@redwood/inference-js/edge'` if they want explicitness.

lucy: Nice. But two follow-ups: 1) how do we avoid Buffer/atob churn in the shared d.ts when we add an edge build? 2) any CI guard we can add to prevent regressions where CJS sneaks back in?

harrison: For types, keep a single runtime-agnostic `dist/index.d.ts` and set top-level "types" in package.json to that file. Avoid referencing `node` types from that file. If you need node-only typings, put them in a separate `index.node.d.ts` and export via the node entry. TS doesn't fully respect conditional exports for types, so explicit separate files + docs are simplest.

ben: For CI, add a small GH action job that runs esbuild with `platform: 'browser'` against the public package entry (or the `/edge` one) and fails if esbuild reports missing resolution or if bundle size grows > threshold. We add a test that tries `import '@redwood/inference-js/edge'` and `new Function('return import("./dist/index.edge.mjs")')()` to simulate runtime resolution.

lucy: Re: Buffer: can we just implement the tiny helpers we need in the edge build (base64 decode/encode, minor Buffer.from/toString) using TextEncoder/TextDecoder and atob/btoa? I want to avoid pulling in the full buffer polyfill.

harrison: Exactly. Implement micro-shims. Example helper: `const b64ToBytes = s => Uint8Array.from(atob(s), c => c.charCodeAt(0))`. For signing use web crypto. Document the limited surface area and export internal helper names only in node build.

build-bot: publish attempt failed 2026-05-02T11:12:03Z: "rollup error: Could not resolve 'fs' imported by dist/index.node.cjs"

lucy: OK action items: Ben - prepare exports + edge entry PR; Harrison - add types guidance and a template `index.edge.d.ts` + ensure top-level types stay node-agnostic; I'll add the esbuild browser-target CI job and add a tiny base64 shim for edge. Will test `import '@redwood/inference-js/edge'` on a sample worker.

ben: Also let's add a short README snippet under `packages/inference-js/README_EDGE.md` with wrangler/esbuild and Vite examples so users know to import `/edge`.

harrison: And a note in docs about idempotency headers for retries from Workers (recommend x-idempotency-key) so retry logic doesn't cause duplicate side effects when CF returns 520/524.

lucy: Thanks team :rocket
